os-io.title: Files and JSON
os-io.summary: Safe paths, everyday file work, file types and JSON with size limits, all in one package with no outside dependencies.

gives.1: Keep every path inside the folder you own, even when a user, a zip file or a config supplies the name.
gives.2: Write files atomically, copy, sync and delete them, and tell what a file really is from its name or its first bytes.
gives.3: Read and write JSON with safe defaults, a byte limit on every read and source-generated overloads.

sample.safe-path: Refuse a path that escapes its folder
sample.kind: Tell a file's type from its first bytes

paths.title: Safe paths
paths.summary: Check that a path stays inside its root, and find the app's own folders.

1.title: Outside names
1.text: A name from outside can hold `..` and point anywhere on the disk.

2.title: Root check
2.text: `PathEx.IsUnder` answers whether a path stays inside a root.

3.title: Full path
3.text: `PathEx.Resolve` turns a relative name into a full path under the root.

4.title: App folders
4.text: `AppPaths` gives the app's data, config and temp folders.

1.title: The risk
1.text: Any name that comes from outside, such as an upload, a zip entry or a setting, can hold `..` and point anywhere on the disk.

2.title: Check and resolve
2.text:
`PathEx.IsUnder` answers whether a path stays inside a root.

`PathEx.Resolve` turns a relative name into a full path under that root or throws an `OSException` with the code `io.path.outside`.

3.title: Path rules
3.text:
Relative names are resolved against the root, not the current folder.

A folder that only shares the root's prefix does not count as inside.

4.title: Folders and codes
4.text:
`AppPaths` gives the app's data, config and temp folders, named after the app.

`IOCodes` lists every error code this package uses.

contain.title: Check whether a path stays inside a folder
contain.note: A sibling folder whose name starts the same way, like uploads-old, is still outside.

resolve.title: Turn a user-supplied name into a safe path
resolve.note: Check the error by its code, not its message; the codes never change.

app-folders.title: Find the app's own folders
app-folders.note: Without a name, the folders are named after the running app.

type.PathEx: Path helpers: containment checks and normalizing.
type.AppPaths: The app's data, config and temp folders. Nothing is created until you ask for it.
type.IOCodes: The error codes of this package, for checking an `OSException` by its `Code`.

PathEx.IsUnder: True when the path is the root itself or inside it. Relative paths are resolved against the root.
PathEx.Resolve: Returns the full path under the root, or throws `OSException` with `io.path.outside`.
PathEx.Normalize: The full path without a trailing separator.

AppPaths.Root: The app's data folder under the user's local app data.
AppPaths.Temp: The app's folder inside the system temp folder.

files.title: Files and folders
files.summary: Write, read, copy, sync and delete files without leaving half-written results behind.

2.title: Atomic writes
2.text: With `atomic: true` it writes a temp file first, then swaps it in.

3.title: Folders
3.text: `DirEx` deletes a folder only when it is inside the root you pass.

4.title: Names and sizes
4.text: `SafeName` cleans file names and `SizeEx` writes sizes the same everywhere.

1.title: Writing files
1.text:
`FileEx.Write` creates the folder it needs and, with `atomic: true`, writes to a temp file first and swaps it in at the end.

So a crash never leaves half a file. Text is written as UTF-8 without a byte order mark.

2.title: Folders
2.text:
`DirEx` makes sure folders exist and lists files as `FileSpec` records.

It deletes a folder only when it is inside the root you pass.

3.title: Names and sizes
3.text:
`SafeName` cleans a name from user input so it is valid on every system.

`SizeEx` writes sizes such as 2.23 MB the same way in every culture.

atomic-write.title: Write a file atomically
atomic-write.note: The settings folder is created on the way.

safe-name.title: Clean a file name from user input
safe-name.note: Names Windows reserves, like CON, get an underscore in front.

sync.title: Copy only the files a backup is missing
sync.note: Files are compared by name, size and last change, so a changed file is copied again.

size.title: Show a size people can read
size.note: The value is cut, not rounded up, and always uses a dot.

type.FileSpec: A snapshot of one file: name, extension, type, MIME type, size and dates. It never reads the disk on its own.
type.SizeUnit: Byte, KB, MB and the larger units, each 1024 times the one before.

FileEx.Write: Writes text, lines or bytes and creates the folder. With `atomic: true` the file is swapped in only when complete.
FileEx.ReadText: Reads the whole file as text. A missing file throws `FileNotFoundException`.
FileEx.Copy: Copies a file and creates the target folder. Pass a `FileSpec` to copy it into a folder.
FileEx.DeleteAsync: Deletes a file, waiting a moment and trying again while another program holds it.
FileEx.SafeName: Removes characters no system allows, trims trailing dots and keeps the name to 100 characters.
FileEx.CanWrite: Tries to open the file for writing, the same way on every system.
FileEx.Sha256: The file's SHA-256 hash as lowercase hex.

DirEx.EnsureFor: Creates the folder a file path needs. Use it when you hold a file path, and `Ensure` when you hold a folder path.
DirEx.Delete: Deletes a folder inside the root you pass. It never deletes the root itself or the folders above it.
DirEx.GetFiles: Lists the files of a folder. With two folders, lists the files the second one is missing or holds in an older version.

SizeEx.ToReadableSize: A size with its unit, like 2.23 MB.
SizeEx.ToSize: The size in a unit you choose, as a number.

types.title: File types
types.summary: Tell what a file is from its name, a URL or its first bytes.

1.title: File type
1.text: `FileTypeEx` maps an extension or a path to a `FileType`.

2.title: MIME types
2.text: `MimeEx` maps file names and URLs to MIME types and back.

3.title: IANA table
3.text: The MIME table follows the IANA registry.

4.title: Real type
4.text: `MimeEx.Sniff` reads the first bytes to find an upload's real type.

1.title: File type
1.text: `FileTypeEx` maps an extension or a path to a `FileType` from one table, in any letter case.

2.title: MIME type
2.text:
`MimeEx` maps file names and URLs to MIME types and back.

The table follows the IANA registry.

3.title: Real type
3.text:
A name only says what a file claims to be.

So `MimeEx.Sniff` reads the first bytes to find the real type of an upload: common images, PDF, ZIP, RAR and GZip.

by-extension.title: Find the type and MIME type from a name
by-extension.note: Unknown extensions give application/octet-stream, the safe default for downloads.

reverse.title: Find the extension for a MIME type
reverse.note: The most common extension comes first.

sniff.title: Check an upload's real type
sniff.note: This upload is named like a JPEG but its bytes are a PNG.

type.FileType: The broad kind of a file, such as Image, Video, Document or Archive.

FileTypeEx.ToFileType: Accepts an extension with or without the dot, or a whole path.

MimeEx.GetMimeType: The MIME type for a file name, or application/octet-stream.
MimeEx.GetMimeTypeFromUrl: Works with full and relative URLs and ignores the query.
MimeEx.GetExtension: The preferred extension for a MIME type. Parameters such as charset are ignored.
MimeEx.Sniff: The MIME type found in the first 12 bytes. A seekable stream is put back where it was.

archives.title: Archives
archives.summary: Zip and unzip with limits, and compress single files with GZip.

1.title: Risky archives
1.text: An archive from outside can fill a disk or write outside its folder.

2.title: Checks first
2.text: `ArchiveEx.Unzip` checks entry count and total size before writing.

3.title: Outside entries
3.text: Any entry that would land outside the target folder is refused.

1.title: The risk
1.text: An archive from outside can be built to fill a disk or to write outside its folder.

2.title: Safe unzip
2.text:
`ArchiveEx.Unzip` checks the number of entries and the total size before it writes anything.

It counts the bytes it actually writes and refuses any entry that would land outside the target folder.

3.title: Single-file GZip
3.text:
`GZip` and `GUnzip` compress one file.

`GUnzip` has the same size limit and removes its output if the limit is hit.

zip-and-unzip.title: Zip a file and unzip it with limits
zip-and-unzip.note: The defaults are 10,000 entries and 1 GiB; pass smaller limits for user uploads.

zip-slip.title: Refuse an entry that escapes the folder
zip-slip.note: This attack is known as zip slip.

ArchiveEx.Zip: Adds a file to a zip, creating it when needed. A file with the same name is replaced.
ArchiveEx.Unzip: Extracts into a folder within the entry and size limits you pass.
ArchiveEx.GUnzip: Decompresses a GZip file, up to a byte limit.

env.title: .env files
env.summary: Load local settings from a .env file into environment variables.

2.title: Skipped lines
2.text: It skips comments and blank lines.

3.title: Environment wins
3.text: A variable that is already set wins unless you pass `overwrite: true`.

4.title: Finding the file
4.text: `Find` also looks in each folder above.

1.title: Reading the file
1.text: `EnvFile.Load` reads `KEY=value` lines, skips comments and blank lines, and removes one pair of matching quotes.

2.title: Which value wins
2.text:
A variable that is already set wins unless you pass `overwrite: true`.

So real environment settings beat the file.

3.title: Finding the file
3.text: `Find` looks for the file in the given folder and then in each folder above it.

load.title: Load a .env file
load.note: SAMPLE_DB_HOST was already set, so only one line was applied.

EnvFile.Load: Applies the file and returns how many variables it set.
EnvFile.FindAndLoad: Finds the nearest .env, loads it and returns its folder, or null.

json.title: JSON
json.summary: Read and write JSON with safe defaults and a size limit on every read.

1.title: Defaults
1.text: `JsonEx` uses camelCase names, enum names and leaves out null values.

2.title: Lenient reading
2.text: It reads comments and trailing commas and ignores letter case in names.

4.title: AOT ready
4.text: Each method also takes a source-generated `JsonTypeInfo<T>`.

1.title: Writing
1.text:
`JsonEx` uses camelCase names and enum names instead of numbers.

It leaves out null values.

2.title: Reading
2.text: It reads comments and trailing commas, and ignores letter case in names.

3.title: Size limit
3.text: Every read, from text, bytes, a stream or a file, stops with `io.json.size` once the input passes `MaxBytes` (10 MB by default).

4.title: Escaping and AOT
4.text:
The default encoder escapes HTML and non-ASCII text so the output is safe inside a web page. Turn on `RelaxedEscaping` for files people read, such as Persian settings.

Each method also takes a source-generated `JsonTypeInfo<T>` for trimmed and AOT apps.

round-trip.title: Write and read JSON
round-trip.note: The empty Note is left out.

persian.title: Keep Persian text readable
persian.note: Use relaxed escaping only for files, never for JSON placed inside HTML.

limit.title: Stop at a size limit
limit.note: The limit counts bytes, so Persian text reaches it sooner than its character count suggests.

append.title: Add an item to a JSON list file
append.note: A broken file stops the call instead of being replaced, and each save is atomic.

source-gen.title: Use a source-generated context
source-gen.note: With a context, only MaxBytes is taken from OSJsonOptions; everything else comes from the context.

type.OSJsonOptions: Per-call settings: MaxBytes, Pretty, RelaxedEscaping and extra converters.

JsonEx.Options: The shared serializer options for a setting. They are cached and read-only.
JsonEx.FromJson: Reads text within the byte limit. A JSON null throws `JsonException`.
JsonEx.ReadAsync: Reads a file through a size-limited stream.
JsonEx.SaveAtomic: Writes the JSON to a temp file and swaps it in.
JsonEx.Append: Adds an item to a JSON array file. It is not locked, so keep to one writer at a time.
